title: nectar
text: main entry point nectar req_prepare(). wraps httr2::request() collection req_* functions single, composable call. provide base URL options need, authentication, pagination, response tidying, req_prepare() stores settings directly request object downstream functions can use automatically. prepare request Crossref /works endpoint. ask ten results per page (rows = 10), select “publisher” “DOI” fields, tell httr2 concatenate select parameter commas (.multi), set cursor parameter "*" trigger cursor-based pagination:

title: nectar
text: Many APIs accept optional key (, Crossref’s case, email address) identify application gain access higher rate limit. nectar provides req_auth_api_key() purpose. can pass req_prepare() via auth_fn auth_args arguments: need remove key (example, fall back anonymous access), pass api_key = NULL:
code: req <- req_prepare(   "https://api.crossref.org/works",   query = list(     rows = 10, cursor = "*", select = c("publisher", "DOI"), .multi = "comma"   ),   auth_fn = req_auth_api_key,   auth_args = list("mailto", api_key = "your@email.com", location = "query") ) req <- req_auth_api_key(   req, # From above, with "your@email.com" attached as the key.   parameter_name = "mailto",   api_key = NULL,   location = "query" )

title: nectar
text: Crossref API returns JSON. nectar’s resp_tidy_json() function parses JSON response body converts result tibble using tibblify::tibblify(). can extract nested path response time subset_path argument. Crossref, actual work items live message$items response body. can attach resp_tidy_json() request via tidy_fn argument req_prepare(), every response automatically tidied call resp_parse() later:
code: req <- req_prepare(   "https://api.crossref.org/works",   query = list(     rows = 10, cursor = "*", select = c("publisher", "DOI"), .multi = "comma"   ),   tidy_fn = resp_tidy_json,   tidy_args = list(subset_path = c("message", "items")) )

title: nectar
text: Crossref uses cursor-based pagination: response contains message$next-cursor field sent cursor query parameter next request. nectar’s iterate_with_json_cursor() generates iterator function pattern, given parameter name path cursor value response body: can attach iterator request via pagination_fn argument req_prepare():
code: iterate_xref <- iterate_with_json_cursor(   param_name = "cursor",   next_cursor_path = c("message", "next-cursor") ) req <- req_prepare(   "https://api.crossref.org/works",   query = list(     rows = 10, cursor = "*", select = c("publisher", "DOI"), .multi = "comma"   ),   tidy_fn = resp_tidy_json,   tidy_args = list(subset_path = c("message", "items")),   pagination_fn = iterate_xref )

title: nectar
text: req_perform_opinionated() performs request. pagination function attached request (), automatically uses httr2::req_perform_iterative() fetch multiple pages; otherwise falls back single httr2::req_perform() call. also applies retry policy handle transient errors. max_reqs argument controls many pages fetch (default: 2). development, keep small. Set Inf confident request works: result always list httr2_response objects additional class nectar_responses, downstream handling consistent regardless whether one many pages fetched.
code: resps <- req_perform_opinionated(req, max_reqs = 2)

code: result <- resp_parse(resps) result
